purpose: Cholic acid is used to treat certain rare liver disorders that children and adults are born with, where the body cannot make bile acids properly. It helps the liver work better and prevents harmful substances from building up. It is also used to treat a condition called peroxisomal disorders that affects how the liver processes fats.
how_it_works: Your body naturally makes bile acids in the liver to help digest fats and absorb vitamins. In some people, a genetic problem means the liver makes abnormal bile acids that can damage it. Cholic acid replaces those harmful bile acids with a healthy one, helping your liver function normally and protecting it from damage.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include diarrhea, stomach pain, nausea, skin itching, and jaundice (yellowing of the skin or eyes). You may also notice changes in your urine color, making it darker than usual. Some people experience reflux or an upset stomach.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, very dark urine, or unusual fatigue, as these could be signs your liver is being affected. Your doctor will check your liver regularly with blood tests while you are on this medication. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can be harmful.
typical_dosing: The dose is based on your body weight and is usually taken once a day by mouth with food. Your doctor will calculate the exact dose for you or your child. The capsules can be opened and mixed with infant formula, breast milk, or soft food if swallowing is difficult.
